speak: In the late nineteenth century, one question had painters, scientists, and horse breeders arguing. When a horse gallops, do all four hooves leave the ground at the same time?
sub: In the late nineteenth century, one question had painters, scientists, and horse breeders arguing. When a horse gallops, do all four hooves leave the ground at the same time?

speak: The human eye couldn't see it. Painters drew it each in their own way.
sub: The human eye couldn't see it. Painters drew it each in their own way.

speak: To settle the doubt, a photographer lined up twelve cameras with threads that the horse snapped as it ran past.
sub: To settle the doubt, a photographer lined up twelve cameras with threads that the horse snapped as it ran past.

speak: The answer was yes. And without meaning to, he opened the door to cinema.
sub: The answer was yes. And without meaning to, he opened the door to cinema.

speak: This is the story of cinema. How still photos learned to move, to speak, and to burst with color.
sub: This is the story of cinema. How still photos learned to move, to speak, and to burst with color.

speak: Chapter one. Twelve cameras.
sub: Chapter one. Twelve cameras.

speak: The experiment was funded by Leland Stanford, a railroad millionaire and horse breeder. Legend says there was a bet involved, though no one could ever prove it.
sub: The experiment was funded by Leland Stanford, a railroad millionaire and horse breeder. Legend says there was a bet involved, though no one could ever prove it.

speak: The photographer was named Eadweard Muybridge. Cameras back then were terribly slow, and it took him years to pull it off.
sub: The photographer was named Eadweard Muybridge. Cameras back then were terribly slow, and it took him years to pull it off.

speak: In eighteen seventy-eight, in front of journalists, a mare named Sallie Gardner ran past the twelve cameras.
sub: In 1878, in front of journalists, a mare named Sallie Gardner ran past the twelve cameras.

speak: In some photos, all four legs were in the air. But tucked beneath her belly, not stretched out like in the paintings.
sub: In some photos, all four legs were in the air. But tucked beneath her belly, not stretched out like in the paintings.

speak: Muybridge did something else: he placed the photos on a wheel and projected them one after another. The horse ran again, now on a wall.
sub: Muybridge did something else: he placed the photos on a wheel and projected them one after another. The horse ran again, now on a wall.

speak: Why do still photos look like a running horse? Because the brain fills in the gaps.
sub: Why do still photos look like a running horse? Because the brain fills in the gaps.

speak: If you see more than ten or twelve images per second, you no longer see photos: you see motion. Just like a flipbook with drawings in the corners.
sub: If you see more than ten or twelve images per second, you no longer see photos: you see motion. Just like a flipbook with drawings in the corners.

speak: There was motion now. What was missing was showing it to a full room.
sub: There was motion now. What was missing was showing it to a full room.

speak: Chapter two. Thirty-three spectators.
sub: Chapter two. Thirty-three spectators.

speak: In the United States, Thomas Edison's team built a box with a peephole: the Kinetoscope. You dropped a coin and watched alone, leaning over, a film just seconds long.
sub: In the United States, Thomas Edison's team built a box with a peephole: the Kinetoscope. You dropped a coin and watched alone, leaning over, a film just seconds long.

speak: In Paris, a photographer named Antoine Lumière saw that box. And he went home with an idea for his sons.
sub: In Paris, a photographer named Antoine Lumière saw that box. And he went home with an idea for his sons.

speak: Auguste and Louis Lumière invented a device that filmed, copied, and projected: the Cinematograph.
sub: Auguste and Louis Lumière invented a device that filmed, copied, and projected: the Cinematograph.

speak: On December twenty-eighth, eighteen ninety-five, they rented the basement of a Paris café. Admission was one franc.
sub: On December 28, 1895, they rented the basement of a Paris café. Admission was one franc.

speak: There were a hundred chairs. Thirty-three people showed up.
sub: There were a hundred chairs. Thirty-three people showed up.

speak: They watched ten short films: workers leaving a factory, a baby eating, a prank on a gardener.
sub: They watched ten short films: workers leaving a factory, a baby eating, a prank on a gardener.

speak: You've probably heard that the audience ran away screaming at an approaching train. That film wasn't in the first screening, and there is no record of panic.
sub: You've probably heard that the audience ran away screaming at an approaching train. That film wasn't in the first screening, and there is no record of panic.

speak: Within a few months, the invention had already reached Buenos Aires, Montevideo, and Mexico City.
sub: Within a few months, the invention had already reached Buenos Aires, Montevideo, and Mexico City.

speak: Thirty-three spectators. The smallest audience in cinema history… and the very first.
sub: Thirty-three spectators. The smallest audience in cinema history… and the very first.

speak: Chapter three. The magician.
sub: Chapter three. The magician.

speak: In the audience that night was a stage magician: Georges Méliès.
sub: In the audience that night was a stage magician: Georges Méliès.

speak: He wanted to buy the machine from the Lumières. They said no. According to legend, they told him cinema was an invention without a future.
sub: He wanted to buy the machine from the Lumières. They said no. According to legend, they told him cinema was an invention without a future.

speak: So he got hold of an English projector and turned it into his own camera.
sub: So he got hold of an English projector and turned it into his own camera.

speak: As he told it, one day he was filming a square when the camera jammed for a minute. When projected, an omnibus suddenly turned into a hearse.
sub: As he told it, one day he was filming a square when the camera jammed for a minute. When projected, an omnibus suddenly turned into a hearse.

speak: He had discovered a trick: if you stop the camera, change something, and keep filming, on screen it looks like magic.
sub: He had discovered a trick: if you stop the camera, change something, and keep filming, on screen it looks like magic.

speak: With tricks like that he made people vanish, multiplied heads, and in nineteen oh-two, sent a spacecraft to the Moon. It lands right in its eye.
sub: With tricks like that he made people vanish, multiplied heads, and in 1902, sent a spacecraft to the Moon. It lands right in its eye.

speak: It was so successful that in the United States they copied it without permission. One distributor even offered to sell Méliès… his own film.
sub: It was so successful that in the United States they copied it without permission. One distributor even offered to sell Méliès… his own film.

speak: Over time, audiences grew tired of his tricks and the war ruined him. He ended up selling toys and candy at a Paris train station.
sub: Over time, audiences grew tired of his tricks and the war ruined him. He ended up selling toys and candy at a Paris train station.

speak: Journalists rediscovered him. In nineteen thirty-one he received the Legion of Honor, presented by Louis Lumière himself.
sub: Journalists rediscovered him. In 1931 he received the Legion of Honor, presented by Louis Lumière himself.

speak: The Lumières filmed reality. Méliès filmed dreams. Cinema needed them both.
sub: The Lumières filmed reality. Méliès filmed dreams. Cinema needed them both.

speak: Chapter four. Hollywood.
sub: Chapter four. Hollywood.

speak: In the United States, the business belonged to a select few. Edison and other companies formed a trust that controlled cameras, film stock, and theaters.
sub: In the United States, the business belonged to a select few. Edison and other companies formed a trust that controlled cameras, film stock, and theaters.

speak: Many producers moved west, to a small California town called Hollywood.
sub: Many producers moved west, to a small California town called Hollywood.

speak: Why there? Because of the sun: you could film almost all year round. And the ocean, mountains, and desert were all close by.
sub: Why there? Because of the sun: you could film almost all year round. And the ocean, mountains, and desert were all close by.

speak: Legend says they were also fleeing Edison's lawyers, and could slip across to Mexico from there. Historians say it's more myth than fact: even the trust's own companies filmed in California.
sub: Legend says they were also fleeing Edison's lawyers, and could slip across to Mexico from there. Historians say it's more myth than fact: even the trust's own companies filmed in California.

speak: Movies were silent, yet almost never quiet: theaters usually had a live pianist or an orchestra playing along.
sub: Movies were silent, yet almost never quiet: theaters usually had a live pianist or an orchestra playing along.

speak: Hollywood wasn't born because of lawyers. It was born because of light.
sub: Hollywood wasn't born because of lawyers. It was born because of light.

speak: Chapter five. The movies talk.
sub: Chapter five. The movies talk.

speak: In October nineteen twenty-seven, The Jazz Singer premiered. It was mostly silent, with title cards. But in a few scenes the star sang and spoke… and the audience heard him.
sub: In October 1927, The Jazz Singer premiered. It was mostly silent, with title cards. But in a few scenes the star sang and spoke… and the audience heard him.

speak: It was the first feature film with synchronized dialogue. Within a few years, silent cinema was over.
sub: It was the first feature film with synchronized dialogue. Within a few years, silent cinema was over.

speak: Where did the sound go? At first, on a separate disc, like a vinyl record, spinning in sync with the projector.
sub: Where did the sound go? At first, on a separate disc, like a vinyl record, spinning in sync with the projector.

speak: Later they put it right on the film strip: a narrow track beside the images. There, sound is a shadow that changes shape.
sub: Later they put it right on the film strip: a narrow track beside the images. There, sound is a shadow that changes shape.

speak: A beam of light shines through it, a sensor reads it… and it turns back into sound.
sub: A beam of light shines through it, a sensor reads it… and it turns back into sound.

speak: So it wouldn't sound strange, the film had to run at a constant speed. Twenty-four frames per second became the standard. We still use it today.
sub: So it wouldn't sound strange, the film had to run at a constant speed. Twenty-four frames per second became the standard. We still use it today.

speak: Twenty-four frames per second were chosen so the human voice wouldn't go out of tune.
sub: Twenty-four frames per second were chosen so the human voice wouldn't go out of tune.

speak: Chapter six. Color and giant screen.
sub: Chapter six. Color and giant screen.

speak: Color arrived slowly. Méliès was already painting some of his films by hand, frame by frame.
sub: Color arrived slowly. Méliès was already painting some of his films by hand, frame by frame.

speak: The real breakthrough came with three colors: red, green, and blue. Mixing those three lights creates almost any color.
sub: The real breakthrough came with three colors: red, green, and blue. Mixing those three lights creates almost any color.

speak: In the nineteen thirties, a camera filmed each color onto a separate strip of film, then combined them. It was called Technicolor.
sub: In the 1930s, a camera filmed each color onto a separate strip of film, then combined them. It was called Technicolor.

speak: In nineteen thirty-nine, The Wizard of Oz began in sepia. When a door opened, the world exploded into color.
sub: In 1939, The Wizard of Oz began in sepia. When a door opened, the world exploded into color.

speak: In the fifties, television stole audiences away from movie theaters. The answer was to do what a TV set couldn't.
sub: In the 1950s, television stole audiences away from movie theaters. The answer was to do what a TV set couldn't.

speak: Huge, wider screens, and even three-D movies with special glasses.
sub: Huge, wider screens, and even 3D movies with special glasses.

speak: And in the seventies, with Jaws and Star Wars, the summer blockbuster was born. Lines wrapped all the way around the block.
sub: And in the 1970s, with Jaws and Star Wars, the summer blockbuster was born. Lines wrapped all the way around the block.

speak: Every time a rival screen appeared, cinema got bigger.
sub: Every time a rival screen appeared, cinema got bigger.

speak: Chapter seven. Twenty-four per second.
sub: Chapter seven. Twenty-four per second.

speak: In the nineties, the computer stepped in. In nineteen ninety-three, the dinosaurs of Jurassic Park looked real. And in nineteen ninety-five, Toy Story became the first feature-length film made entirely on a computer.
sub: In the 1990s, the computer stepped in. In 1993, the dinosaurs of Jurassic Park looked real. And in 1995, Toy Story became the first feature-length film made entirely on a computer.

speak: Then even the film strip disappeared: today, almost everything is shot and projected digitally.
sub: Then even the film strip disappeared: today, almost everything is shot and projected digitally.

speak: And the highest-grossing movies in history now make nearly three billion dollars.
sub: And the highest-grossing movies in history now make nearly three billion dollars.

speak: Yet every movie you watch—in a theater, on TV, or on your phone—is still the exact same thing: still images, one after another. Twenty-four per second.
sub: Yet every movie you watch—in a theater, on TV, or on your phone—is still the exact same thing: still images, one after another. Twenty-four per second.

speak: Your brain does the rest, just like with that horse. And cinema is still looking for the same thing as in that Paris basement: for a group of strangers, in the dark, to watch the same light.
sub: Your brain does the rest, just like with that horse. And cinema is still looking for the same thing as in that Paris basement: for a group of strangers, in the dark, to watch the same light.

speak: Cinema is still a horse that, for a single instant, flies.
sub: Cinema is still a horse that, for a single instant, flies.
